docs.summary:
Handles copy / paste-as-new / paste-values for individual components, using Echo serialization. The payload lives on the system clipboard as text so it survives a scene swap - which matters, because [`PrefabEditingMode`](#api~Prowl.Editor.GUI.SceneView.PrefabEditingMode) discards and reloads the whole scene on enter/exit. That's what makes "copy in prefab mode, paste into the scene" work. Payload format (first line is a header so the type can be peeked without parsing the body):

```csharp
ProwlComponent:<AssemblyQualifiedName>
{ ...serialized component... }
```

Scene-object references (fields typed GameObject / Component / Transform, at any depth) are linked by persistence id rather than serialized by value: [`SceneReferenceResolver`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.SceneReferenceResolver) is handed to Echo as the context's external-reference resolver, so Echo emits a stable key for them instead of deep-cloning the target into an orphan, and resolves that key back to the live instance on paste. References that can't be resolved (different scene, deleted object) become null.
Serialize a component onto the system clipboard.
The component type currently on the clipboard, or null if the clipboard holds something else or the type can't be resolved in this project. Cheap enough to call from menu-build code.
True if the clipboard holds a component that can be pasted as a new component.
True if the clipboard holds a component of exactly `type`.
Add the clipboard component to `go` as a new component, with undo. Returns the new component, or null if the clipboard is empty/unusable.

Overwrite `target`'s field values from the clipboard, with undo. The target keeps its own identifier, GameObject and sibling index - only data is replaced. Requires the clipboard type to match exactly.
